title: PermissionState
description: `GET /sessions/:sessionId/permissions/:requestId`: the state of one permission request, for a client that was told about it by somebody else — a push may be minutes late, so the app asks before it renders (plan 02, D-22). In the domain this is a discriminated union by `status` (`pending` carries `request` and `remainingExtensions`; `resolved` carries the rest), which the generator cannot express as a `oneOf`; flattened here with every field but `status` optional, paired by `status` (plan 28, B-48). `request` is carried as a generic open object — exactly `permission.requested`'s payload — rather than a precise nested shape, because the domain type behind it (`Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>`) is already open at the TypeScript boundary.

request.description: Present exactly when `status` is `pending`. Exactly the `permission.requested` payload — the card renders from this and nothing else.

remainingExtensions.description: Present exactly when `status` is `pending`. What stops a card offering an extension that no longer exists.

requestId.description: Present exactly when `status` is `resolved`. The request that was settled.

auto.description: Present exactly when `status` is `resolved`. The server decided it, with nobody answering.

resolvedBy.description: Present when `status` is `resolved` and a human answered.

resolvedFrom.description: Present when `status` is `resolved` and a human answered.

toolUseId.description: Present when `status` is `resolved` and the engine named a tool call.

via.description: Present when `status` is `resolved` and nobody was asked.

answers.description: Present when `status` is `resolved`, the request was a question and the decision `allow`.

interaction.description: Present when `status` is `resolved` and the request was a question — the phone a push opened draws it with what was answered.
